description: Make the whole worklog UI responsive from a 390px phone up to desktop, without changing how it looks at desktop widths. The user tested the work item peek on a phone: the totals labels clip ('Horas equivalent', 'Horas apontadas'), 'R$ 0,00' wraps inside its box, and the allowance title 'Bolsa de horas do chamado' collides with the '161% consumido' badge. The cause is fixed column counts and non-wrapping flex rows with no breakpoints. Every change is additive Tailwind responsive prefixing: the classes that apply at md and above must remain what they are today so the desktop layout is untouched.
steps: Study the fork's existing responsive convention before writing classes: apps/web/core/components/service-reports/consumption-tab.tsx, operational-tab.tsx and billing-tab.tsx all use `grid grid-cols-2 gap-6 rounded-lg border border-subtle p-4 md:grid-cols-4`. Mirror that shape (mobile-first base class, md: for the desktop count) rather than inventing a new one, and keep using the fork tokens (border-subtle, bg-surface-2, text-custom-text-350, etc.).

apps/web/core/components/service-logs/service-log-totals.tsx: replace the fixed `grid gap-2 ${cards.length === 4 ? 'grid-cols-4' : 'grid-cols-3'}` container with a responsive one - 2 columns on phones, the current 3 or 4 from md up. Give each card `min-w-0` so a grid item can actually shrink, let the label wrap instead of clipping (drop any nowrap, add `leading-tight`), and make the value survive a long string ('R$ 12.345,67', '1h 52min 30s') with `break-words` and a size step such as `text-sm md:text-base`. The Tooltip wrapper must stay the direct grid child so the columns still line up.

apps/web/core/components/service-logs/service-allowance-indicator.tsx: (a) the header row `flex items-center justify-between gap-2` must wrap on a phone so the consumed-percentage badge drops under the title instead of colliding with it - add wrapping and keep the title block `min-w-0` with a wrapping (not truncating) title, while the badge cluster stays `shrink-0`; (b) the figures container `grid grid-cols-3 gap-2` becomes responsive - the three labelled figures (creditado / consumido / restante) must each keep their label and value readable at 390px, so use fewer columns on mobile and restore `grid-cols-3` from sm or md up; (c) give the figure values `break-words` so '-2h 30min' and a long human duration do not overflow; (d) leave the progress bar and the alert boxes visually identical at desktop, but check the alert text block already wraps (it is `flex items-start gap-1.5` with an icon marked shrink-0 - confirm the span can wrap and add `min-w-0` if it cannot).

apps/web/core/components/service-logs/service-log-section.tsx: the section header is `flex items-center justify-between` and can hold four Buttons (Editar, Excluir, Bolsa de horas, Adicionar apontamento). Let the header wrap and let the action cluster wrap and align to the end, so on a phone the title takes one line and the buttons flow onto the next instead of squeezing. Do not remove or hide any button and do not change the permission conditions around them.

apps/web/core/components/service-logs/service-log-list-item.tsx: the entry row is `flex items-start justify-between gap-2` with a text column and a right-hand cluster of up to four badges plus the edit and delete icon buttons. Make the two blocks stack on a phone (or let the row wrap) with the action cluster still reachable and right-aligned at desktop, allow the badge cluster itself to wrap, and keep `min-w-0` on the text column. The per-segment line is already `flex flex-wrap` - verify the badges inside it (billing type, overridden hour type) do not force overflow, and that the description keeps `break-words whitespace-pre-wrap`.

apps/web/core/components/service-logs/service-log-client-section.tsx: the totals grid is already `grid-cols-2 sm:grid-cols-3`, so here the work is the cards and rows - add `min-w-0`/`break-words` to the card value, and make the row header (`flex items-center justify-between gap-2` holding the hours and the date) wrap or shrink so neither is cut. The metadata line is already `flex flex-wrap`; confirm it stays that way.

apps/web/core/components/service-logs/service-log-form.tsx: the interval pair (start_time / end_time, `flex gap-3`) and the catalogue dropdown pair (hour type / billing type, `flex gap-3`) must stack on a phone and stay side by side from sm up. Also check the entry-mode toggle (`flex w-fit`) and the footer button row still fit at 390px inside the modal.

apps/web/core/components/service-logs/service-log-modal.tsx and the four other modals in the folder (credit-service-allowance-modal.tsx, edit-service-allowance-modal.tsx, delete-service-allowance-modal.tsx, delete-service-log-modal.tsx): confirm ModalCore's EModalWidth value behaves at 390px (read packages/ui's ModalCore implementation to see whether the width classes are already responsive) and reduce the inner `p-5` padding on mobile if the content is pinched. Only change what is actually cramped, and say in findings what you checked and left alone.

apps/web/core/components/issues/peek-overview/view.tsx: the side-peek/modal content wrapper is `relative flex flex-col gap-3 space-y-3 px-8 py-5`, spending 64px of a 390px viewport on horizontal padding. Make the horizontal padding responsive (small on phones, the current px-8 from md up) for both content branches. In the full-screen branch, the right rail is a hard `!w-[400px] flex-shrink-0` next to a scrolling column: make that layout stack (or the rail full width) below md while keeping the exact current desktop geometry. Touch nothing else in this file - it is a core Plane component shared by every work item.

Re-read every file you touched and confirm no desktop-width class changed meaning: for each edit, the classes in effect at md and above must be the same set that was there before (a base class you added must be overridden at the breakpoint). At a 390px viewport the reasoning holds for each of the four reported defects: totals cards sit two per row with wrapping labels, the monetary value has room for 'R$ 0,00' on one line, the allowance title and the consumed-percentage badge are on separate lines, and no text sits outside its bordered box.

The classes in effect from md up are unchanged for every file touched, so the desktop layout is byte-for-byte equivalent in rendered geometry (verifiable by diffing the class strings and confirming each addition is a mobile-only base with a md:/sm: restoration).
The peek side-peek/modal content padding is responsive and the full-screen right rail no longer forces a 400px column below md, with the desktop geometry of both preserved.

findings:
COMMIT 776176f6f on fix/worklog-horas-legiveis-e-responsivo. 8 files, +127/-46. All web checks green (types exit 0, oxlint 0 warnings 0 errors on the touched paths, i18n untouched and in sync). No translation file was added or changed, so no new i18n key was needed: every fix is layout, not copy.

METHOD. There is no browser in this sandbox, so each change was verified by reading the emitted class string and reasoning about the breakpoint, as context.json requires. The rule applied everywhere: the classes in effect from the breakpoint up are the exact set that was unconditional before, so the desktop layout is unchanged; the added base class only applies below it. Two Tailwind facts do the actual work and are worth carrying forward: (a) a grid item and a flex item both default to `min-width: auto`, so they refuse to shrink below their content and push text OUT of the bordered box -- that, not a missing `truncate`, is what produced the reported 'Horas equivalent' clipping, and `min-w-0` is the fix; (b) `flex-wrap` cannot change a row that already fits, which is why the wrapping rows below needed no `sm:flex-nowrap` counterpart to keep desktop identical.

PER-FILE TABLE (mobile = <640px, tablet = sm 640-767px, desktop = md 768px+)

1. service-logs/service-log-totals.tsx -- the four totals cards.
   mobile: `grid-cols-2`, cards `min-w-0`, label `leading-tight` and wrapping, value `text-sm break-words`. Four cards become 2x2; 'Horas equivalentes' wraps to two lines inside its border; 'R$ 0,00' fits one line (~155px of card, ~131px inside px-3).
   tablet: same as mobile (2 columns). This is a deliberate choice, not an oversight: at 640px the peek is still `w-full` and four columns would be ~150px each, which is where the labels started clipping in the first place.
   desktop: `md:grid-cols-4` / `md:grid-cols-3` and `md:text-base` -- byte-identical to the previous unconditional `grid-cols-4`/`grid-cols-3` and `text-base`.
   Tooltip stays the direct grid child: `Tooltip` defaults to `renderByDefault`, so it `cloneElement`s the card with a ref and adds NO wrapper element (checked packages/ui/src/tooltip/tooltip.tsx). The grid child really is the card div, so `min-w-0` lands on the grid item.

2. service-logs/service-allowance-indicator.tsx -- header, figures, alerts.
   mobile: header row gained `flex-wrap` (gap stays `gap-2`, so the existing gap doubles as the row gap) -- 'Bolsa de horas do chamado' takes line 1 and the '161% consumido' badge drops to line 2 instead of colliding; the title gained `break-words` and wraps rather than truncates, because half a title is worse than two lines of it; the figures grid is `grid-cols-2` (creditado + consumido on row 1, restante on row 2) with `min-w-0` cards and `break-words` values so '-2h 30min' stays in the box; the inherited line and both alert boxes gained `min-w-0 break-words` on the text span beside their `shrink-0` icon.
   tablet: `sm:grid-cols-3` restores the three figures on one line; header still wraps only if it must.
   desktop: identical to before -- `sm:grid-cols-3` IS the old `grid-cols-3`, the header row never wraps because the title and badge fit, and the progress bar and alert boxes were not touched.

3. service-logs/service-log-section.tsx -- section header with up to four Buttons.
   mobile: `flex-wrap` + `gap-y-2` on the header and `flex-wrap justify-end` on the action cluster. Title on line 1, the buttons flow onto the next line(s). No button is hidden and NO permission condition was touched (`canCreditAllowance`, `hasLoadedAllowance`, `canLogTime` are unchanged) -- hiding an action on a phone would make the feature unusable there rather than merely ugly.
   tablet/desktop: unchanged. Only a ROW gap was added, never a column gap, so the space available to the row is exactly what it was; `flex-wrap` is inert while the row fits.
   Note: the husky hook's oxfmt reflowed the long `canCreditAllowance && ...` condition and the two Button calls onto multiple lines. That is why this file's diff is 44 lines for a 2-class change. No behaviour changed.

4. service-logs/service-log-list-item.tsx -- one work log entry.
   mobile: the row is `flex-col gap-2`, so the reading block and the badge/action cluster stack; the cluster is `flex-wrap` so four badges plus the edit and delete buttons flow onto a second line and stay reachable.
   tablet: `sm:flex-row sm:items-start sm:justify-between` + `sm:shrink-0` restores the original single row.
   desktop: identical (`sm:` restores every class that was unconditional). Verified without changing them: the per-segment line was already `flex flex-wrap`, and the description already carried `break-words whitespace-pre-wrap`.

5. service-logs/service-log-client-section.tsx -- the R11 client projection.
   mobile: the totals grid already had `grid-cols-2 sm:grid-cols-3`, so only the cards needed work -- `min-w-0`, `leading-tight` label, `break-words` value; the per-row header (hours + date) gained `flex-wrap` so the two never cut each other now that the hours read '1h 52min 30s' instead of '1,875h'; the description span gained `break-words`.
   tablet/desktop: unchanged. The metadata line was already `flex flex-wrap` and stays that way. No field was added or removed, so R11 is untouched.

6. service-logs/service-log-form.tsx -- the two paired rows.
   mobile: the interval pair (start_time/end_time) and the catalogue pair (hour type/billing type) are `flex-col`, so each takes the full 318px of modal content width. The `type="time"` controls have a browser-imposed minimum width (the stepper is part of the control) and did not fit two-up.
   tablet/desktop: `sm:flex-row` restores the original `flex gap-3` exactly.
   Checked and left alone: the entry-mode toggle (`flex w-fit`, two ~100px buttons = ~200px, fits), the footer button row (Cancel + Submit, fits), and the date/duration/description fields which are already single-column.

7. service-logs/service-log-modal.tsx -- the work log modal shell.
   mobile: inner padding `p-4`, giving 8px back to the widest form in the folder.
   tablet/desktop: `sm:p-5`, the original.
   ModalCore was READ, not changed: the panel is `w-full` with a `sm:max-w-*` cap and already caps its height with `max-h-[calc(100dvh-5rem)] md:max-h-[calc(100dvh-10rem)]`, and `EModalPosition.TOP` adds `mx-4`. So at 390px the panel is 358px wide and scrolls internally -- the width and height are already responsive and needed nothing. Only the content was pinched.
   Checked and deliberately left alone: credit-service-allowance-modal.tsx and edit-service-allowance-modal.tsx keep `p-5` -- their fields are single-column full-width Inputs and a textarea, nothing competes for horizontal space; delete-service-allowance-modal.tsx and delete-service-log-modal.tsx use `AlertModalCore`, which is already mobile-first in packages/ui (`flex flex-col items-center gap-4 p-5 sm:flex-row sm:items-start` and a `flex-col-reverse ... sm:flex-row sm:justify-end` footer).

8. issues/peek-overview/view.tsx -- the shared core Plane peek. Two branches, nothing else touched.
   side-peek/modal branch, mobile: `px-4` instead of `px-8`. The peek is `w-full` below md (`md:w-[50%]` in peekOverviewIssueClassName), so `px-8` was spending 64px of a 390px viewport on padding; this is the single change that gave every child 32px back. tablet: `px-4` still (the peek is still full width at 640px). desktop: `md:px-8`, and md is exactly where the peek narrows to 50%, so the geometry is the one it always had.
   full-screen branch, mobile: the outer row is `flex-col`, the 400px properties rail becomes `w-full` with `border-t`, and both columns drop `h-full` so the already-scrolling parent handles the height. 400px simply does not exist on a 390px screen.
   tablet: still stacked (md is the breakpoint, matching the side-peek). desktop: `md:flex-row md:h-full md:!w-[400px] md:border-t-0 md:border-l` -- exactly the previous class set. The legacy leading-`!` important syntax was KEPT and verified to still compile under Tailwind 4.1.17 (compiled `!w-[400px]` and `md:!w-[400px]` through tailwindcss/dist/lib.mjs and both emit `width: 400px !important`), which is what lets `md:!w-[400px]` beat the new `w-full` base regardless of source order. Do not 'modernise' it to `w-[400px]!` without re-checking, and do not drop the `!`: without it `w-full` would win.

issue-detail/main-content.tsx -- CHECKED, NOT CHANGED, as the step allows. It renders the ServiceLogSection as a plain sibling inside a fragment with no width constraint and no horizontal row around it. Its own container lives in issues/issue-detail/root.tsx: `h-full w-full space-y-6 overflow-y-auto px-9 py-5`, which is 72px of padding at any width, leaving 318px on a 390px phone. The two non-wrapping rows inside main-content.tsx (the type switcher row and the reaction row) hold short controls and are unrelated to the work log.

review_response:
Answering the review at .agents/tasks/task-worklog-humanize-hours-and-responsive/2026-08-10-200538-review.md (verdict NEEDS_CHANGES). This field covers the layout half: issues 4, 5, 6 and 10, plus the missing decision entry the review noted in 'Deliberately left alone'. Issues 1, 2, 3, 7, 8 and 9 are answered in FEAT-002.json.

ISSUE 4 - the breakpoints described the viewport while the peek is half of it. FIXED, with container queries, which is the first option the review offered and the one the repo already uses (settings/content-wrapper.tsx, settings/profile/modal.tsx). The review's arithmetic was right and the defect was real: `md:` fires at 768px, which is the exact width where `peekOverviewIssueClassName` takes the side peek to `md:w-[50%]`, so four columns at a 768px viewport left ~50px of card interior against ~151px at 390px -- the mid-range band was worse than the phone case.
What changed:
- `service-log-section.tsx` and `service-log-client-section.tsx` declare `@container` on their root, and `service-allowance-indicator.tsx` declares its own (it has `px-3`, and its figures grid must be measured against the space INSIDE that padding). Nested containers are fine: an `@` variant resolves against the nearest declaring ancestor.
- `service-log-totals.tsx`: `md:grid-cols-4|3` -> `@xl:grid-cols-4|3` (36rem = 576px) and `md:text-base` -> `@md:text-base` (28rem = 448px).
- `service-allowance-indicator.tsx`: `sm:grid-cols-3` -> `@sm:grid-cols-3` (24rem = 384px).
- `service-log-client-section.tsx`: `sm:grid-cols-3` -> `@md:grid-cols-3`.
- `service-log-list-item.tsx`: `sm:flex-row sm:items-start sm:justify-between` and `sm:shrink-0` -> the same four classes at `@xl` (576px), which is about what the old `sm:` (640px viewport) really had available inside the peek (~584px).
The breakpoints are arithmetic, not taste, and each number is in a code comment: 4 cards at 576px of container = (576-24)/4 = 138px per card, 114px inside `px-3`, enough for '1h 52min 30s' at text-base (~96px); 3 allowance figures need ~110px each plus two 8px gaps = 346px, so 384px is the first honest size.
The resulting side-peek behaviour (container = peek width minus the content padding): 390px viewport -> 358px container -> 2 columns; 768 -> 320 -> 2 columns (this is the case the review called worse than the bug, and it is now the phone layout); 1024 -> 448 -> 2 columns at text-base; 1280 -> 576 -> 4 columns with 114px of card interior; 1920 -> 896 -> 4 columns, identical to before. Full-screen mode at 1280 gives the content column 816px -> 4 columns; at 768, where the 400px rail is present, 304px -> 2 columns. The full work item page is wide at every desktop size, so it keeps 4 columns.
`service-log-form.tsx` and `service-log-modal.tsx` were deliberately NOT converted, agreeing with the review: `ModalCore` is portalled and sized against the viewport, so `sm:` there means what it says. `ServiceLogForm` is only ever rendered inside `ServiceLogModal` (checked).
COMPILATION VERIFIED, because a container-query variant that does not compile fails silently to the mobile layout: every new class was run through tailwindcss 4.1.17's own compiler (node_modules/.pnpm/tailwindcss@4.1.17/.../dist/lib.mjs, `compile()` with `@import "tailwindcss"`). `.@container` emits `container-type: inline-size`; `@sm/@md/@xl` emit `@container (width >= 24rem/28rem/36rem)`; `order-first`, `md:order-none`, `border-b`, `md:border-b-0`, `max-w-full` and `md:!w-[400px]` (still `width: 400px !important`) all emit. Both branches of the dynamic `${cards.length === 4 ? '@xl:grid-cols-4' : '@xl:grid-cols-3'}` exist as literals in the source, so Tailwind's scanner sees them.
CONTAINMENT CHECKED, since `container-type: inline-size` implies `contain: layout style inline-size`: (a) all three roots fill their parent (stretched flex items in a `flex-col`, or block-level in `issue-detail/root.tsx`), so inline-size containment cannot collapse them -- it would matter only for a content-sized element; (b) `contain: layout` makes an element the containing block for absolute/fixed descendants, and there are none inside these components (grep for absolute/fixed/sticky finds nothing but a comment); (c) `@plane/ui` Tooltip renders through @blueprintjs/popover2, which portals to the body, and every modal goes through headlessui's Dialog portal, so no popup is positioned against a container.

ISSUE 5 - full-screen peek buried the properties rail on a phone. FIXED with `order-first md:order-none` on the rail, which is the review's own suggestion. Below `md` the rail (state, assignees, dates) now comes BEFORE the content column instead of after the description, the work log and the activity feed; from `md` up `order-none` restores the original right-hand position. The separator moved with it: `border-t`/`md:border-t-0` became `border-b`/`md:border-b-0`, so the line still sits between the two blocks rather than floating above the first one. `md:border-l` is untouched, and so is the `!` in `md:!w-[400px]` -- verified again through the compiler above, and the comment saying not to drop or 'modernise' it stays.

ISSUE 6 - the `flex-wrap` comments overstated the guarantee. FIXED by correcting the comments, not by adding `sm:flex-nowrap`. Both rows now say that `flex-wrap` is unconditional at every width, that a row which fits is laid out exactly as before, and that a row which does not fit -- four buttons plus a long translated title, or a long allowance reference -- now wraps where it used to overflow, which is the better of the two failure modes. Adding `flex-nowrap` at a breakpoint would restore the overflow the review itself calls the worse outcome, so the honest fix was the sentence, not the class. Same category, already flagged by the previous pass: `leading-tight` on the card labels also applies at desktop; it changes a single-line label's line box by about a pixel and cannot reflow anything, and `md:leading-normal` would be a wrong 'restoration' because Tailwind's `text-xs` ships its own 1.333 line-height.

ISSUE 10 - report insight cards were not hardened for the longer strings. FIXED. `report-insight-card.tsx` sits directly in the reports' `grid grid-cols-2 ... md:grid-cols-4` and had no `min-w-0` on its root -- a grid item defaults to `min-width: auto`, so with `w-fit text-20 font-bold` on the value a three-term duration like '1234h 34min 4s' could push the card past the column. The root is now `flex min-w-0 flex-col gap-2`, the value button is `w-fit max-w-full ... break-words` (keeping `w-fit` so only the number is the click target for the drill-down) and the label carries `break-words`. These dashboards are full-page and not inside a peek, so their own `md:grid-cols-4` stays a viewport breakpoint, which is correct there.

THE MISSING DECISION - the review noted that D68 covered only the hour rendering and the responsive reasoning lived in code comments. FIXED: docs/worklog/DECISOES.md gained D69, in Portuguese and in the same voice, with the 'Resumo do que muda no codigo' table the surrounding entries use. It records why viewport breakpoints were the wrong tool inside the peek (with the 768px versus 390px numbers), the container sizes and the arithmetic behind each, the rule for when a viewport breakpoint is still right (a portalled modal), the two load-bearing details (`md:!w-[400px]`'s bang and `order-first md:order-none`), what was deliberately left alone, and that the verification is class-string reasoning because this fork has no browser and no JS test runner.

STILL DELIBERATELY LEFT ALONE, and named so the next reader does not think it was missed:
- `issues/issue-detail/root.tsx` keeps `px-9` at every width (72px of a 390px screen). It is core Plane geometry affecting the title, the description editor and the activity feed identically, and with `min-w-0`, `break-words` and the container-query grids the section survives the 318px that remain. Recorded in D69 as a candidate for its own decision.
- The `modal` peek mode is `size-5/6` at every width. At 390px that is ~325px, and with `px-4` the section gets ~293px, which the two-column layout handles.
- The six `<table>` elements in service-reports / service-pricing have no horizontal-scroll wrapper. They are Admin dashboards on the full page, not reachable from the work item peek, and giving them `overflow-x-auto` plus a `min-w` is a real change to a screen this task did not touch.
